extracted.intended_audience: GAP users and developers (computational algebra users, package authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference-manual guidance for constructing and manipulating domains, iterators, and element-level operations in GAP, including required functions, attributes, mutability semantics, and category/structure rules. Intended to guide GAP package authors and advanced users in correct use and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterator behaviour on list changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes concerning positions that have not yet been reached in the iteration will also affect the iterator; e.g., if a list is enlarged then the iterator will iterate also over the new elements at the end of the changed list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that changes of list will also affect all shallow copies of list. This applies to iterators that iterate over collections implemented as lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: TrivialIterator
rubrics_metrics.description: TrivialIterator(elm) is a mutable iterator for the collection [elm] that consists of exactly one element elm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended for trivial one-element iteration (see IsTrivial reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: IteratorByFunctions required components
rubrics_metrics.description: IteratorByFunctions(record) returns a (mutable) iterator for which NextIterator, IsDoneIterator, and ShallowCopy are computed via prescribed functions provided as components of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record must contain functions: NextIterator(iter) (updates iter and returns next element), IsDoneIterator(iter) (returns done-status), and ShallowCopy(iter) (returns record usable to create an independent iterator behaving the same under NextIterator/IsDoneIterator). Additional optional components: ViewObj and PrintObj for printing. Further data components may be present.

rubrics_metrics.name: IteratorByFunctions mutability and copy semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: IteratorByFunctions does not make a shallow copy of record; this record is changed in place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the record is modified in place, care must be taken when reusing the same record. Iterators constructed with IteratorByFunctions are in the filter IsStandardIterator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain as structured set
rubrics_metrics.description: Domain is GAP’s name for structured sets: a domain has a set of elements and an operational structure (a collection of operations under which the domain is closed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: groups, rings, fields. Elements exist independently of the domain; domains often are constructed as closures of given generators under the operational structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational structure vs properties
rubrics_metrics.description: The operational structure of a domain is fixed at construction, whereas properties (like associativity or commutativity) can be discovered later and are not automatically added to the operational structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if all inverses happen to lie in a monoid, the operational structure does not change to a group unless the domain was constructed as such. The operational structure determines applicable operations; properties discovered later influence IsStruct tests and behavior but do not alter the original Struct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generation and Struct constructor semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Struct(arg1,arg2,...) functions construct domains as the closure of given generators under the specified operational structure; Struct first checks IsGeneratorsOfStruct([info,]gens) and returns fail if the check fails.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the check is omitted, call Struct ByGenerators directly. Generators must be appropriate for the intended structure (e.g., cannot use permutations as vector-space generators).

rubrics_metrics.name: GeneratorsOfStruct attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: For a domain D with operational structure corresponding to Struct, the attribute GeneratorsOfStruct returns a list of corresponding generators of D (may require D to 'know' some generators to compute them).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There can be multiple notions of generation for a domain; generators may depend on other information (e.g., underlying field for vector spaces). If a domain is printed as Struct([a,b,...]) and has the attribute, GeneratorsOfStruct(D) is guaranteed to equal [a,b,...].

rubrics_metrics.name: Struct ByGenerators vs Struct WithGenerators
rubrics_metrics.description: Struct ByGenerators implements construction from generators; Struct WithGenerators guarantees that the returned domain's GeneratorsOfStruct value equals the provided gens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use WithGenerators when you need the returned domain to explicitly remember the given generators as its GeneratorsOfStruct value.

rubrics_metrics.name: ClosureStruct
rubrics_metrics.description: ClosureStruct(D,obj) returns the smallest domain (w.r.t. Struct) that contains D as subset and obj as element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to construct domains from an existing domain by adjoining elements or subdomains under the operational structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: AsStruct semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: AsStruct([info,]D) returns a domain E that has the same elements as D and the desired operational structure if D is closed under that structure; otherwise returns fail. The info argument provides extra information if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: AsVectorSpace(GF(2), D) can change the underlying field view. When no extra info is required, AsStruct acts as an attribute.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsomorphismRep Struct
rubrics_metrics.description: IsomorphismRep Struct(D) returns a mapping hom from D to a domain E having the structure Struct and representation Rep if such an isomorphism exists; otherwise returns fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: IsomorphismPermGroup returns an isomorphism to a permutation group for finite groups; IsomorphismPcGroup returns to a pc-group if polycyclic. Useful to change representation for efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain categories and implication hierarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: Each operational structure Struct has an associated domain category IsStruct; implications between these categories describe the hierarchy (e.g., IsMagmaWithInverses implies IsMagmaWithOne, a field is a commutative division ring, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common implications: IsDomain implied by each domain category; IsMagma implied by categories describing closure under multiplication; additive and multiplicative hierarchies described. The operational-structure hierarchy determines applicable functions and filters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting and semantics of Parent/SetParent/HasParent
rubrics_metrics.description: It is possible to assign to a domain D a parent P containing D as subset via SetParent(D,P); if D already has a parent, SetParent calls are ignored. HasParent checks for a parent; Parent(D) returns the parent or D itself if none is set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SetParent triggers UseSubsetRelation and allows storing parent-relative attributes (e.g., NormalizerInParent). Parent cannot be changed once set. Some functions (e.g., Subgroup) return domains with parent pre-set; these functions do not guarantee a specific parent in all cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing subdomains: Substruct, Substruct NC, AsSubstruct, IsSubstruct
rubrics_metrics.description: Substruct(D, gens) constructs subdomains (e.g., Subgroup) of D generated by gens and sets Parent(S)=D; Substruct NC omits the subset check; AsSubstruct constructs AsStruct(S) then sets parent to D; IsSubstruct checks both IsStruct and subset via IsSubset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NC suffix to skip membership checks when appropriate. IsSubstruct may be unnecessary if only subset relation is required; there are specialized IsSubset methods for various structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic attribute for families and objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Characteristic(obj) returns the characteristic of obj: for a family of additive-with-zero elements it's the least positive n with IsZero(n*x) for all x, otherwise 0. For collections families it inherits characteristic from underlying family; for other objects characteristic may be undefined or fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characteristic is defined only for suitable families and objects in the appropriate filters; behavior may vary and return fail or errors for unsupported types.

rubrics_metrics.name: One (multiplicative identity) operations and mutability semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: OneImmutable, OneMutable, OneSameMutability return the multiplicative neutral element of obj, differing in mutability: OneImmutable returns an immutable result; OneMutable returns a new mutable object if available; OneSameMutability returns a value matching the argument's mutability when possible. One and Identity are synonyms of OneImmutable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One is applicable to domains only if they are a magma-with-one (IsMagmaWithOne); One may call Representative if HasOne(D) is true. OneOp is synonym for OneMutable. Default One for multiplicative elements calls OneMutable (methods for OneMutable must not delegate to One).

rubrics_metrics.name: Zero (additive identity) operations and mutability semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: ZeroImmutable, ZeroMutable, ZeroSameMutability return the additive neutral element of obj with the same mutability distinctions as One variants. ZeroSameMutability(obj) is equivalent to 0 * obj. Zero is synonym of ZeroImmutable; ZeroOp synonym of ZeroMutable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Zero applies only if obj is an additive magma-with-zero (IsAdditiveMagmaWithZero); otherwise use AdditiveNeutralElement. Default Zero for additive elements calls ZeroMutable (methods for ZeroMutable must not delegate to Zero). For domains, Zero may call Representative only if HasZero(D) is true.

rubrics_metrics.name: MultiplicativeZeroOp
rubrics_metrics.description: MultiplicativeZeroOp(elt) returns a multiplicative zero element z in the family F of elt such that z * m = z = m * z for all m ∈ F, if such an element can be determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Families in IsMultiplicativeElementWithZero often arise from adjoining a new zero to an existing magma (see InjectionZeroMagma or MagmaWithZeroAdjoined). Example usage shown for group with 0 adjoined.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsOne / IsZero / IsIdempotent properties
rubrics_metrics.description: IsOne(elm) is true iff elm = One(elm); IsZero(elm) is true iff elm = Zero(elm); IsIdempotent(elt) returns true iff elt is its own square (even if IsZero returns true).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are properties used to test element identities and idempotency; they rely on the corresponding One/Zero definitions for the element/family.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inverse operations and mutability semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: InverseImmutable, InverseMutable, InverseSameMutability return the multiplicative inverse of elm (or fail if not invertible). Differences are mutability semantics: InverseImmutable returns immutable, InverseMutable returns a fresh mutable object when available, InverseSameMutability returns mutable if elm is mutable and a mutable version exists. InverseSameMutability(elm) is equivalent to elm^-1. Inverse and InverseOp are synonyms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The default method of InverseImmutable calls InverseMutable (methods for InverseMutable must not delegate to InverseImmutable). Note mapping invertibility: a general mapping is invertible w.r.t. Inverse only if its source equals its range; use InverseGeneralMapping for bijections with differing source/range.

rubrics_metrics.name: AdditiveInverse operations and mutability semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: AdditiveInverseImmutable, AdditiveInverseMutable, AdditiveInverseSameMutability return the additive inverse of elm with analogous mutability variants. AdditiveInverseSameMutability(elm) is equivalent to -elm. AdditiveInverse is synonym of AdditiveInverseImmutable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default AdditiveInverse method calls AdditiveInverseMutable (methods for AdditiveInverseMutable must not delegate to AdditiveInverse).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order attribute for elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Order(elm) is the multiplicative order: the smallest positive integer n such that elm^n = One(elm) if such n exists. If the order is infinite, Order may return the value infinity or may run into an infinite loop testing the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful with infinite-order elements; computing order can be non-terminating in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison operations \= and \<
rubrics_metrics.description: \=(left-expr,right-expr) and \<(left-expr,right-expr) are the underlying operations for equality and ordering; <> <= > >= delegate to these operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In general objects in different families cannot be compared with \<. See Section 4.13 for reasons and exceptions; methods can be installed for these operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: CanEasilyCompareElements and CanEasilySortElements properties
rubrics_metrics.description: CanEasilyCompareElements(obj)/Family indicate whether elements in the family fam of obj can be easily compared with \=; CanEasilySortElements indicates efficient total ordering via \< and implies CanEasilyCompareElements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default method asks the family and returns false by default. Use CanEasilyCompareElementsFamily to query without computing result. If a family can compare elements ab initio, it should set the property as an implied filter for correctness and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic operation symbols and extensibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Binary arithmetic operations \+, \*, \/, \^, \mod are defined as underlying operations for which methods can be installed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For special methods for \*, \/, \^, and \mod consult the appropriate index entries. Implementations should provide efficient methods for types where special behavior is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: LeftQuotient operation
rubrics_metrics.description: LeftQuotient(elm1,elm2) returns the product elm1^(-1) * elm2, sometimes more efficient than computing the inverse then multiplying for certain types (e.g., permutations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide LeftQuotient methods for types where direct computation is cheaper than separate inverse and multiplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comm (commutator) operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Comm(elm1,elm2) returns the commutator defined as elm1^-1 * elm2^-1 * elm1 * elm2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example usage shown for permutations; implementers should follow the defined algebraic formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: LieBracket operation
rubrics_metrics.description: LieBracket(elm1,elm2) returns elm1 * elm2 - elm2 * elm1. Addition is assumed associative (not necessarily commutative); multiplication not assumed commutative or associative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use in contexts where bracket operations are meaningful (Lie algebras); be aware of assumptions about associativity/commutativity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sqrt operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Sqrt(obj) returns a square root x such that x*x = obj; if multiple choices exist, the choice depends on the type of obj (type-specific methods determine which root is returned).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ER is the Sqrt method for rationals. Implement type-specific Sqrt methods to specify canonical choices when multiple square roots exist.
